subject: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE

messages.author: ab4c9ed2cd29563b
messages.subject: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
parts:
For various reasons it would be nice to have more access to some of the (excellent) plots that MSstats can produce. The current `dataProcessPlots()` and `groupComparisonPlots()` functions have the argument `address=FALSE` which will print a single graph to the RStudio viewer, but assignment of the output of either function returns NULL.

It would be better if this assignment operation returned the ggplot object for further manipulation. I have done some initial investigation, and I have some rough idea of how this could be done. The functions typically have an `if (address != FALSE){}` section. This could be followed by an `else { return(pfinal) }` block, however the `print(pfinal)` line in the preceding `for` loop is problematic.

messages.author: 542668c56342d060
messages.subject: Re: Return ggplot objects for dataProcessPlots and groupComparisonPlots when address=FALSE
parts:
Hi Jason, You can also take the output of the dataProcess() function and extract the dataframe which is used to make the ggplot figures. I've pasted some code that I've used to make my own ggplot figures from MSstats data.

# dataProcess of ProteomeDiscoverer data
quant_pd <- dataProcess(input_pd,
                        logTrans = 2,
                        normalization = FALSE,
                        nameStandards = NULL,
                        address = "",
                        fillIncompleteRows = TRUE,
                        featureSubset = "all",
                        remove_noninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,
                        n_top_feature = 3,
                        summaryMethod = "TMP",
                        equalFeatureVar = TRUE,
                        censoredInt = "NA",
                        cutoffCensored = "minFeature",
                        MBimpute = TRUE,
                        remove50missing = FALSE,
                        maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999,
                        clusters = NULL)

# creating dataframes of output
processed_data <- quant_pd$ProcessedData
rl_data <- quant_pd$RunlevelData

# Lowercase column names
names(processed_data) <- tolower(names(processed_data))
names(rl_data) <- tolower(names(rl_data))

#### Plots

# Boxplot of feature data before normalization
ggplot(processed_data %>% filter(censored == FALSE, Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(run), y = log2(intensity)))

# boxplot of feature data after normalization
ggplot(processed_data %>% filter(censored == FALSE, Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = factor(run), y = abundance, fill = group_original))

# boxplot of protein data
ggplot(rl_data %>% filter(Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = originalrun, y = logintensities, color = group_original)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# bargraph of protein ids
ggplot(rl_data %>% filter(Contaminant == FALSE)) +
  geom_bar(aes(x = originalrun, fill = group_original)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Best,

Josh
